The score rates a night on the measurable dimensions of sleep health (Buysse 2014): how long, how unbroken, how regular and when you slept.

# The parts
- Duration, 40 points: time asleep against your need, your usual sleep kept between 7 and 9 hours. Nothing below 60 % of your need. Duration has the broadest evidence for health and performance.
- Continuity, 25 points: the National Sleep Foundation's quality criteria. Full points for a sleep efficiency of at least 85 %, at most 20 minutes awake after falling asleep, at most 30 minutes to fall asleep and at most one awakening of 5 minutes or more.
- Regularity, 25 points: the middle of the night within 30 minutes of your usual earns full points, two hours off earns none. Irregular sleep predicts mortality more strongly than short sleep (Windred 2024).
- Timing, 10 points: the middle of the night between 02:00 and 04:00, the sleep health criterion. Two hours outside earns nothing.

# What is not scored
- Sleep stages: wrist sensors tell them apart only roughly, and one night's shares say little about its quality.
- Brief arousals: they are a normal part of healthy sleep.

# Ratings
- 85 and above: good
- 70 to 84: fair
- Below 70: poor

# Compared with Fitbit
Fitbit's score also counts deep and REM sleep, restlessness and sleeping heart rate, with weights it does not publish, so the two can differ by 10 to 20 points. Resting heart rate and HRV count in readiness instead.

The stages as your watch estimated them from movement and heart rate.

- Deep sleep: the most restorative stage, mostly early in the night.
- REM sleep: dreaming sleep, longer towards the morning.
- Light sleep: about half of a normal night.
- Awake: short awakenings are normal; several a night are part of healthy sleep.

The typical shares are for healthy adults. Compared with a sleep lab, wrist sensors misplace a good part of stage time, so read single nights loosely and look at trends.

Measured while you slept and compared with your own normal.

- HRV: the median of the watch's five-minute values, as Fitbit reports it. The normal range is your 60-day average plus or minus half a standard deviation, in place once there are 14 nights.
- Resting heart rate: as your watch derived it from the night. Usual is the average of the last 30 nights.
- Breathing rate: breaths per minute during sleep. A clear rise above usual is a common early sign of illness.

When you slept over the last two weeks, one bar per night from going to bed to getting up.

- Bars that line up mean a regular rhythm, which counts for the regularity part of the score.
- Tap a night to see it.
